tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, ensure the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg is either empty or has a larger top disk. Without this, you may move a non‑top disk or place a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you generate a move, check both source and destination constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, or moving disk 5 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, so use it to temporarily hold a peg while you move larger disks. Without this, you may run out of legal moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by a smaller one, move the smallest disk to a free peg before proceeding.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving disk 1 on a peg that blocks moving disk 3, causing a dead‑end.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining tower on top. Without this, you may unnecessarily move already‑correct disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal peg already has a correctly ordered suffix of the final tower.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 off the goal peg even though it is already at the bottom of the final tower.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto its goal peg after the larger ones are already correctly positioned. Without this, you may place a larger disk on top of a smaller one later.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final configuration, start with the largest disk and work downwards.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 before ensuring disk 3 is already on the goal peg, leading to a later illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the last syntactically correct list of moves in the response is the complete move sequence. Without this, the verifier may read an incomplete or malformed list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After generating the solution, place the full move list as the final list in the output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing a move list that is followed by extra text or an incomplete list, causing the parser to stop early.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the output within the model’s token budget. Without this, the answer may be truncated and rejected.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the problem size is large or the naive solution would produce many moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing an excessively long move list that gets cut off, resulting in an empty or incomplete answer.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the move list, mentally simulate each move from the initial configuration to ensure the final arrangement equals the goal. Without this, you may output a sequence that stops short or misplaces disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the answer, run through the moves step‑by‑step.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg because the final state was not checked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a destination peg using the third peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest of the k, then move the k‑1 stack onto the destination. Without this, you may not find a systematic way to relocate sub‑towers.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to relocate a contiguous block of disks that are already in order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a three‑disk sub‑tower by moving each disk individually without recursion, leading to many unnecessary moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid blocking future moves with temporary placements
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When using a disk as a temporary buffer, place it on a peg that will not need to be cleared for moving larger disks later. Without this, you may later have to move the temporary disk again, increasing move count or causing illegal configurations.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During planning of intermediate moves, choose a peg that will stay free for subsequent larger‑disk moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Putting the smallest disk on the auxiliary peg that you later need empty to move a larger disk, forcing extra shuffling.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, ensure the peg's top disk is larger than the moving disk (or the peg is empty). If a smaller disk blocks the target, move that smaller disk elsewhere first. Without this, the move would violate size ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the destination peg already contains disks and the top disk is smaller than the disk you intend to move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, without first relocating disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generating before emitting any moves, often due to token limit or premature termination.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always ensure that a move list is produced, even if empty, and keep generating until the list is complete.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the size rule when focusing on moving disks toward the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before adding a move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may select a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg, overlooking the top‑only rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before adding the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may run out of tokens or stop early, leaving the move list unfinished.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Monitor token usage and, if needed, generate the move list in a compact form; verify that the final list ends with a closing bracket.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of disk locations after several moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an internal representation of the current configuration and update it after each move.
